1.explanation: All four files participate in parsing and re-printing YAML front-matter inside Markdown. unified-plugins/front-matter.js injects the front-matter parser into the remark pipeline, parse.js reads the raw YAML and hands it off to a JS object, and print.js stringifies that object back to YAML—unfortunately normalizing away blank lines. Finally printer-markdown.js glues the printed YAML back into the Markdown document. The blank-line removal happens because parse.js/print.js rely on a YAML stringifier that drops inter-item spacing, and printer-markdown.js simply splices that output back without preserving the original empty lines.
1.bug_scenario: When running Prettier 3.3.0 on a Markdown file that contains YAML front-matter with intentionally spaced-out list items, Prettier’s formatting pipeline silently strips all blank lines inside the front-matter sequence. In our example (the “Real Projects” front-matter), the empty lines between `- name: Mr.Hope’s Blog`, `- name: Mo7’s Blog`, and `- name: Guo’s Page` are removed after `prettier.format(input, { parser: "markdown" })`. We lose visual separation between entries even though the user deliberately inserted those blank lines.

2.explanation:
All three files are part of the frontmatter pipeline.  

• src/utils/front-matter/parse.js: This splits the raw Markdown into frontmatter and content but (mistakenly) trims or discards leading/trailing blank lines inside the YAML block.  

• src/utils/front-matter/print.js: This reassembles the frontmatter block for output. Because the parser already removed blank lines, the printer never reintroduces them, leading to missing empty lines in the final formatted output.  

• src/language-markdown/unified-plugins/front-matter.js: This plugin hooks the frontmatter into the Markdown AST. It uses the parse/print utilities above and may normalize or overwrite the raw YAML node value—further preventing preservation of the user’s original blank lines.  

Fixing the bug requires adjusting `parse.js` to preserve all empty lines inside the `---` section and updating `print.js` to emit them verbatim, and ensuring the unified plugin does not strip them out during AST transformations.
2.bug_scenario:
When formatting Markdown files containing YAML frontmatter, Prettier 3.3.0 incorrectly removes some of the user’s blank lines inside the `---` header block. In the reproduction, the user had intentional empty lines before the `blogs:` section (and between its items), but after running `prettier --parser markdown`, those empty lines were gone.

The attached screenshots illustrate a site (Mo7’s blog demo) built from Markdown files: you can see the author’s intended spacing in the YAML frontmatter is no longer reflected on the page after formatting.
